requirements_summary: Goal: Production-grade dedicated capacity for low-latency advisory chat and reranking. Non-streaming LLM API calls (batch responses) and streaming token-by-token flows. Targets: p50/p95/p99 must be defined separately for streaming vs non-streaming. Must support VPC, KMS, audit logs, EU data residency. Throughput: 200 concurrent chat sessions, median request size ~120 tokens, peak 1.2k reqs/min. Cost-sensitivity moderate; willing to reserve for predictability. Need deterministic reserved planning (how many GPUs to reserve for given SLOs).
sla_terms_summary: Requested: latency SLOs tied to production traffic shape with monthly measurement windows. Proposed SLOs (starting point): non-streaming end-to-end client-observed p50 < 150ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 1200ms; streaming token emission latency p50 < 30ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 600ms. Uptime SLA 99.9% for dedicated pool. Credits: sliding scale tied to measured SLO misses; legal asks for minimum sample-size clause and exclusion windows for maintenance and force majeure. Need explicit definition of measurement endpoints and instrumentation (server response-time, server-first-byte, client full-response).
measurement_plan: Dual-sided timing: install Redwood agent hooks in POC to capture server_received_ts, server_response_start, server_response_end; advise Emberlake to capture client_sent_ts and client_received_ts for correlation
Define measurement windows: 5-minute rolling percentiles, aggregate monthly for SLA; require minimum 1000 samples per day for valid percentile assertions
Synthetic replay for POC: replay recorded production traces (drive:/perf/emberlake/latency-trace-sample.jsonl) and synthetic spike tests at 2x expected peak
Track streaming token latency separately: emit per-token timestamps, aggregate token-latency histograms; ensure token-level p95 computed over tokens, not over requests
Account for batching and KV cache state: run tests with warm cache and cold-cache passes; report both and surface warm-cache SLO as primary
Include network e2e probes (client side) and server-side tracing to attribute tail latency to network, batching, or kernel stalls
latency_alignment_notes: Key alignment items from 2026-03-02 workshop: agree that 'p95' will be computed over successful responses only, exclude retries and client timeouts; streaming p95 measured on token emission intervals; the customer wants client-side dashboards in addition to Redwood Console. Decided to add 60s warmup exclusion window for pod restarts. Redwood to provide sample Kibana/Datadog dashboards and SLO query templates. SE recommended percentile smoothing (sliding window 5m) and to report both raw and smoothed percentiles for transparency.
reserved_gpu_planning: Initial recommended reservation: equivalent of 8xA100 for baseline (predictable throughput for 200 concurrent sessions and p95 targets). Sizing rationale: assumed model = 40B quantized fp16/qat, avg seq len 160, average throughput ~75 tokens/sec per GPU under continuous batching; include 20% headroom for burst. Plan includes optional burst pool (2 GPUs) billed as overage with fixed burst rate. Next step: run benchmark with customer's model/quantization and token mix to finalize commit level.
poC_success_criteria: 1) non-streaming p95 meets agreed target under 1x and 2x peak traffic during 48h run; 2) streaming token p95 meets target; 3) consistent KV cache hit improvements observed; 4) infra and KMS integrations validated; 5) legal sign-off on SLA draft
negotiation_points: 1) precise metric definitions (server vs client) and measurement windows; 2) minimum sample size and exclusion clauses; 3) burst capacity pricing and rollback policy; 4) credits calculation and remediation timelines; 5) audit log retention and data residency evidence
